description.value: This multicenter study examined 18F-FDG PET measures in the differential diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease, frontotemporal dementia, dementia with Lewy bodies, mild cognitive impairment, and normal aging using standardized automated voxel-based analysis.
The study was a multicenter observational comparison of healthy elderly individuals and patients with MCI, AD, FTD, and DLB recruited at seven participating centers.

18F-FDG PET has been proposed as a suitable modality to support the early and differential diagnosis of dementia (3).
18F-FDG PET

Pet of the cerebral metabolic rate of glucose (CMRglc) is increasingly used to support the clinical diagnosis in the examination of patients with suspected major neurodegenerative disorders, such as Alzheimer’s disease (AD), dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB), and frontotemporal dementia (FTD).

source_definition.value: Voxelwise Z score defined as (subject mean − normative database mean) / normative database standard deviation, relative to an additional database of 55 longitudinally confirmed normal elderly individuals.

model_settings.value: Scans were realigned to the anterior-posterior commissure line, spatially normalized to the Talairach and Tournoux atlas using a 12-parameter affine transformation followed by nonlinear warping, yielding 2.25-mm voxels. Each scan was compared with a normative database while controlling for global activity using Neurostat scaling; voxelwise Z scores were thresholded at P ≤ 0.01 one-sided, corresponding to Z ≥ 2.33.

software.value: Neurostat (Neurological Statistical Image Analysis), University of Washington, processed on a Sun workstation; SPSS version 12.0 was used for statistical analyses.

spans.text: 18F-FDG PET scans were transferred to a Sun workstation (Sun Microsystems Inc.) and processed at New York University using the Neurological Statistical Image Analysis (Neurostat; University of Washington) standard diagnostic routine (30,31).
